answer: A topological protocol maps peer interactions into a trust atlas, scoring identity autonomy via a graph kernel that penalizes dense synthetic subgraphs. Nodes maintain reputation by answering a periodic beacon pulse through multi-hop latency proofs. An attacker incurs a verifiable cost in physical routing infrastructure and geographically distributed bandwidth per identity. However, collusive rings can still blend into honest clusters, and high-latency edge nodes risk accidental exclusion.
